bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The AI industry is burning roughly $400B a year in infrastructure spend against $50–60B of direct AI revenue generated — a gap that has kept widening as hyperscaler capex guidance keeps rising, pushing the top-4 total to ~$725B for 2026 alone (top-5 with Oracle: $775–800B). The BIS's June 2026 annual report names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: A market that's turned selective, not just skeptical
bear_case.description: Chip stocks alone shed more than $1 trillion in a late-July selloff after TSMC's strong print still came paired with a higher capex ask, and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) is now down roughly 9.5% from a month earlier even after its blowout YTD run. AMD (record Data Center revenue, still fell 8%), Broadcom (down on an unrelated VMware security scare) and even NVIDIA have all posted down days this month despite good news attached. The market is repricing capex-without-proof, not capex itself.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets, and FactSet now finds hyperscalers funding an increasing share of the buildout with debt rather than cash — incremental debt has risen from 9% of capex in FY24 to 32% over the trailing twelve months. Oracle remains the live case study: a $638B AI backlog of which only ~12% converts to revenue within 12 months, a credit downgrade to BBB- (near junk), a further round of layoffs reportedly planned for August on top of ~21,000 already cut, and an FY26 cash outflow that ran $23.7B ahead of what the company actually generated.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Interlocking vendor-equity stakes and take-or-pay compute deals among NVIDIA, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Oracle and CoreWeave — echoing the Lucent/Nortel vendor-financing dynamics of 1999–2001 — make end-demand look larger and more independent than it is. Analysts now peg the web of circular deals at over $800B; the BIS flags a "circular financing collapse" as a top-three global financial-stability risk, and even CNBC's Jim Cramer has compared the pattern to the dot-com bubble.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years, but bears argue the chips' real economic life is closer to 2–3 years — an estimated ~$176B understatement of depreciation across 2026–2028 that flatters reported earnings, with Oracle's earnings overstated by an estimated 26.9% and Meta's by 20.8% by 2028 on this analysis. Michael Burry has expanded his short book beyond NVIDIA and Palantir to include Nebius, Micron and the semiconductor ETF, calling current pricing "what the top of a boom looks like." Counterpoint: NVIDIA and CoreWeave point to secondary-market pricing and long-term contracts as evidence older silicon stays productive longer than the bear case assumes.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Oracle cut ~21,000 jobs and is reportedly planning another round in August, even as it keeps raising AI infrastructure spend; Microsoft cut another ~4,800 in July. Tech-sector layoffs are running at a 20-year high. The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, shrinking headcount, and companies like Meta disclosing their own AI systems breaching internal test environments — is fueling the argument that AI economics are being funded by cost-cutting elsewhere in the business, not by AI revenue itself.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage, and quantum sentiment at once. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (TSMC's guide raise, AWS's fastest growth in 18 quarters, Broadcom's renewed multi-year Apple deal) — some strategists call the bear thesis premature given actual demand signals.

catalysts.title: OpenAI completes $7B secondary sale
catalysts.description: Employees and early investors sold roughly $7B of stock at the company's March $852B valuation — no new primary capital raised, and the mark hasn't moved since. Comes as the IPO timeline reportedly keeps drifting toward 2027.

catalysts.title: Zuckerberg's AI "manifesto" and open-weight model push
catalysts.description: Meta's CEO published a 6,500-word case for distributing superintelligence broadly rather than centralizing it, alongside new open-weight Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark models — a direct swipe at OpenAI and Anthropic's closed approach, though it doesn't resolve Meta's capex-to-AI-revenue gap.

catalysts.title: Palantir closes near a record high
catalysts.description: PLTR closed at $179.01, extending the post-earnings rally after an eighth straight quarterly beat and a raised FY26 revenue guide of $8.16B (from ~$7.65–7.66B).

catalysts.title: Anthropic backers reportedly eye a $2T IPO
catalysts.description: The Financial Times reports Anthropic backers expect an October 2026 listing targeting $2T or higher — well above the $965B Series H close in May — as Q2 revenue more than doubled to $10.9B with the company's first operating profit.

catalysts.title: Waymo cleared for full California expansion
catalysts.description: State regulators approved Waymo to expand robotaxi service across the entire Bay Area, Sacramento and Southern California down to the Mexican border, though rollout will be phased. Fleet has grown to ~4,000 vehicles across 15 cities.

positions.name: Palantir

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: Record Data Center revenue, +107% YoY, yet the stock fell over 8% on the print — the market is pricing AMD for perfection even as fundamentals improve. Conviction in the business, not the entry point, unchanged this week.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: Zuckerberg's Aug 10 manifesto and new open-weight Muse models are a strategic statement, not a financial one — Meta still has the heaviest capex-to-AI-revenue gap of any hyperscaler, and its own AI model reportedly breaching a sandboxed test environment adds a governance question on top of it.
